turns.message: I am an adult in North Dakota changing my own first and last name in a standalone petition unrelated to divorce. Please guide me through standard name-change preparation with publication.

outcome.text:
I’ll help you prepare a North Dakota adult name-change petition using the **standard publication track**.

Because you are changing your last name, your packet includes:

- Petition
- Declaration
- Notice of Petition for Name Change
- Confidential Information Form
- Proposed Order

The filing fee is **$160**. Publication in the official newspaper for your county is required, and the judge generally cannot consider the petition until **30 days after publication**. [source:68571ed7-eb72-4719-b206-ab8eab6d59a0]

**First action item:** Before filing, call the Clerk of District Court for the county where you have lived for the past six months and ask:

> “Does the judge require a criminal history background check before I file, or after I file?”

The timing varies by judge, and a background check can take several weeks. Use the North Dakota court locator: https://www.ndcourts.gov/court-locations

The Petition and proposed Order generally become part of the public court record and show your current legal name and requested name. The Confidential Information Form is sealed. Leave the case number blank because the clerk assigns it, and do not sign the proposed Order because only the judge signs it. [source:68571ed7-eb72-4719-b206-ab8eab6d59a0]

We’ll prepare one fact at a time. **What is your current legal first name?**

grounded.text:
North Dakota’s adult name-change materials do not state how recent a criminal-history check must be when you file. The timing also varies by judge. Before requesting one, call the Clerk of District Court for the county where you will file and ask:

> “Does the judge require a criminal-history background check before I file, and how recent must the check be?”

The county clerk can also tell you whether the check is required before filing or after filing. You can find the clerk through the [North Dakota court locator](https://www.ndcourts.gov/court-locations). The court materials state that a required check can take several weeks and that you pay its cost. [source:68571ed7-eb72-4719-b206-ab8eab6d59a0]

questions.without_corpus:
In North Dakota, the criminal-history check for an adult name-change petition must generally be **conducted within 30 days before you file the petition**. It should be submitted with the petition.

This requirement is under **N.D.C.C. § 32-28-02**. Because court procedures can change, confirm the timing with the district court clerk or the North Dakota Legal Self Help Center before filing.

questions.question: Will the North Dakota court always hold a hearing for an adult name change?

grounded.text:
No. North Dakota does **not** presumptively require a hearing for an adult name change. However, the judge may decide that a hearing is needed. If one is scheduled, the Clerk of District Court will send you the date, time, and location. [source:68571ed7-eb72-4719-b206-ab8eab6d59a0]

A hearing is separate from the possible criminal-history background check. Before filing, call the clerk in the county where you have lived for the past six months and ask whether the judge requires that check before or after filing.

questions.without_corpus:
No. A North Dakota court does **not necessarily hold a hearing** for every adult name-change petition. The judge may decide the petition based on the filed documents, but may schedule a hearing if more information is needed, if there is an objection, or if local court procedures require it.

Check the notice from the clerk or judge carefully. If a hearing is scheduled, you generally must attend unless the court specifically excuses you. North Dakota’s name-change procedures are governed primarily by **N.D.C.C. §§ 32-28-01 through 32-28-03**, and practices can vary by district.

questions.question: I lived in two North Dakota counties during the last 12 months. Where must I publish my adult name-change notice?

grounded.text:
For the standard adult name-change track, publish the notice in the **official newspaper of the North Dakota county where you currently reside and are filing**. You must have lived in that county for at least the past six months. You do not generally publish in both counties.

The notice form identifies the newspaper as the official newspaper in the county where you reside. [source:68571ed7-eb72-4719-b206-ab8eab6d59a0]

If your move means you have not lived in your current county for six months, call the **Clerk of District Court** before filing. North Dakota’s materials say to file in the county where you have lived for the past six months. [source:68571ed7-eb72-4719-b206-ab8eab6d59a0]

questions.without_corpus:
For an adult name change in North Dakota, the notice generally must be published **once a week for four consecutive weeks in a legal newspaper in the county where you currently reside and file the application**. Living in another North Dakota county during the prior 12 months does **not ordinarily require publication in both counties**.

You should confirm the filing county and an approved legal newspaper with the district court clerk, especially if you recently moved or have not established residency there. Publication may be waived or restricted in certain protected-person circumstances.

questions.question: Does Burleigh County offer a same-day adult name-change service for an extra $25?

grounded.text:
I could not verify that Burleigh County offers a same-day adult name-change service for an extra $25. The North Dakota court material lists a **$160 filing fee**, but it does not list a same-day service or an additional $25 fee. [source:68571ed7-eb72-4719-b206-ab8eab6d59a0]

Call the **Burleigh County Clerk of District Court** to confirm whether the local clerk offers any expedited processing and whether an additional fee applies. The North Dakota court locator is available here: https://www.ndcourts.gov/court-locations

Also, a judge may require a criminal-history background check, and timing varies by judge. The court advises asking the clerk whether that check is required before or after filing.
